However, the complex and costly nature of these multicomponent systems and the low stability and activity of these systems make larger scale reactions challenging. Thermophilic P450s from bacteria and archaea have been identified but have low activity when reconstituted using electron transfer partner proteins and surrogate oxygen donors. We demonstrate that two cytochrome P450 enzymes (CYP119A1 and CYP119A2) from hyperthermophilic archaea can be engineered to be efficient peroxygenase enzymes requiring only hydrogen peroxide to function. Catalytic oxidation was achieved through modification of three residues in the dioxygen binding groove, including the important addition of a proline residue after the glutamate acid/base residue which significantly enhanced the activity (8-fold over the double mutant and three orders of magnitude over the natural enzyme). These peroxygenases oxidised tridecanoic acid with high activity and enabled further investigation of the substrate range of these enzymes. Both enzymes could oxidise fatty acids and related compounds as well as styrene and the norisoprenoid β-ionone. The oxidation of these substrates occurred with excellent regioselectivity. The CYP119A2-QEP variant was stable to heating at 85-90 °C, had higher activity at 70 °C, could tolerate up to 20 % v/v acetonitrile and was able to catalyse ≥1000 total turnovers across the range of substrates tested. These new peroxygenase biocatalysts, provide hyperthermostable enzyme scaffolds to enable selective and catalytic oxidation of inert C-H bonds using a single enzyme system and cheap cofactors.

item.title: Photoresponsive Co3S4 Nanocrystals
item.description: Colloidal semiconductor nanocrystals offer opportunities for solution-processable optoelectronic devices, although their functionality depends on electrical transport across interparticle junctions. Co3S4 has been explored largely for electrochemical applications. Here, we investigate optoelectronically active colloidal Co3S4 quantum dots (QDs) for lightresponsive electrical devices. Structural characterization confirms crystalline spinel Co3S4 nanoparticles with a mean diameter of 8.8 ± 3.1 nm. Optical absorption extends into the infrared region, with an estimated optical band gap of 0.35 eV. Films deposited onto Au interdigitated electrodes exhibit unstable current–voltage characteristics and no discernible photo response before post-deposition treatment. Following treatment with a butylamine–isopropanol mixture, the films show improved electrical reproducibility and a measurable photo response under broadband illumination, with rise and decay times of 15.8 and 31 s, respectively. These findings establish that structurally pure Co3S4 QDs grown through the colloidal route, could be used for optoelectronics.

item.title: Complementary Roles of Iodide-Mediated Pathways and Anion Dynamics in Lithium-Ion Transport in Li3PS4-LiI Glasses
item.description: LiI addition enhances lithium-ion transport in sulfide glasses, yet the microscopic mechanisms linking halide incorporation to faster conduction remain unclear. Here, we investigate how LiI promotes Li+ migration in (100−x)Li3PS4–xLiI glasses by resolving changes in local structure, migration energetics, and anion dynamics. A machinelearning potential trained on newly generated ab initio molecular dynamics data and an existing sulfide-electrolyte dataset enables 10 ns simulations of approximately 5000atom glass models at 300 K over a LiI content range of 0–50 mol%. The potential is validated against density functional theory calculations, experimental densities, and X-ray total scattering profiles. Although the PS4 3–units remain intact and their time-averaged inter-unit correlations change little, Li+ diffusivity more than doubles across this composition range, accompanied by increased migration beyond local cage-like regions. To characterize the energetics of these pathways in a disordered environment, we introduce an analysis that combines Voronoi partitioning into P-and I–-centered domains with atomic potentialenergy fluctuations along Li+ trajectories. The resulting statistical local energy-barrier indicators allow comparisons between domain transitions without assigning absolute activation energies. This analysis reveals two complementary effects of LiI addition. Transitions involving I–-centered domains exhibit lower barrier indicators than direct transitions between P-centered domains, identifying favorable I–-mediated migration pathways. LiI addition also lowers the barrier indicators for direct P-to-P transitions, extending its influence beyond pathways that pass through I–-centered domains. Enhanced local translational and rotational dynamics of PS4 3–units accompany this broader reduction, suggesting that anion motion helps facilitate Li+ migration. These findings explain how LiI can enhance transport while largely preserving the average glass structure and highlight the combined roles of local migration pathways and anion dynamics in designing sulfide glass electrolytes.

item.title: Development and Validation of Low-Temperature Partitioning Extraction Methods for Multiresidue Determination of Pesticides in Soil and Surface Water
item.description: Two complementary low-temperature partitioning methods were systematically optimized and validated for the multiresidue determination of five chemically diverse pesticides in soil and surface water by HPLC-UV. A 23 factorial design was used to evaluate the effects of extraction solvent volume, agitation time, and ionic strength on pesticide recovery. Acetonitrile volume was the primary factor, and the optimization established harmonized conditions for solid–liquid (SLE-LTP) and liquid–liquid (LLE-LTP) extraction: 6 mL acetonitrile, 1 min vortexing, and no salt addition. The simplified procedures reduced solvent consumption by 25–50% compared with selected previously reported methods, while achieving recoveries of 78–106% and relative standard deviations ≤13%. AGREEprep scores of 0.54 (SLE-LTP) and 0.53 (LLE-LTP) indicated comparable environmental performance. The applicability of both methods was further evaluated using real environmental samples, demonstrating the feasibility of harmonizing sample preparation across distinct matrices while maintaining satisfactory analytical performance.

item.title: Cristobalite-Type Compounds for Rechargeable Potassium-Ion Batteries
item.description: Potassium-ion batteries have emerged as high-voltage and economically advantageous electrochemical energy storage systems with promise to viably complement and/or augment lithium-ion technology owing to the natural abundance, projected low cost and favourable redox potential of potassium. Their continued advancement, however, is primarily predicated upon the discovery of electrode and electrolyte materials adept to delivering high energy density, long-term cycling stability and rigorous safety performance. Cristobalite-type compounds have recently garnered traction as prospective candidates, for these materials not only combine theoretically high energy density with structural robustness but can also be designed exclusively from earth-abundant and low-toxicity constituent elements. This Review provides a critical assessment of the rapidly expanding family of cristobalite-type compounds, which exhibit pronounced structural versatility and the capacity to reversibly intercalate two potassium ions per formula unit, thereby enabling high theoretical energy densities. We particularly survey recent advances in their structural chemistry, electrochemical behaviour and potassium-ion transport properties, and elucidate the mechanistic principles that govern their electrochemical performance. Finally, we outline future research directions, encompassing rational materials design, advanced characterisation methodologies and large-scale computational screening, to optimise cristobalite-type compounds as high-performance electrode materials and solid-state electrolytes for potassium-ion batteries.

item.title: Non-Symmetric Stapling of Tyrosine-Containing Peptides Driven by Intramolecular Non-Covalent Interactions
item.description: Non-symmetric stapling of native peptides that crosslinking two distinct residues is a valuable tool for enriching diversity of peptide macrocycles, yet it is less achieved due to the high demand for chemo- and siteselectivity control, as well as the competitive intermolecular peptide crosslinking. Herein, we reported a noncovalent interaction activation strategy for non-symmetric stapling of tyrosine-containing peptides by employing ethenesulfonyl fluoride (ESF) as a bifunctional crosslinker. Once covalently anchored to peptide, the sulfonyl fluoride motif is activated by non-covalent interactions, which triggers an intramolecular SuFEx click reaction with tyrosine to afford peptide macrocycles. This approach efficiently crosslinks diverse residue pairs, including Cys–Tyr, His–Tyr and Pro–Tyr. Notably, the protocol is scalable and can be performed in solid-phase synthesis, providing a robust access to tyrosine-bridged peptide macrocycles with excellent diversity.

item.title: Generic OH• Scavenging Constants in UV/H2O2 Screening: Size and Direction of the Error Across Four Published Datasets
item.description: Generic literature rate constants are widely used to estimate hydroxyl-radical (OH•) scavenging in UV/H2O2 screening when no matrix-specific probe measurement is available. The reliability of that shortcut is usually assumed rather than tested. Using four independently published datasets, this study compares generic-constant scavenging estimates with experimentally informed references to establish the size and direction of the error. On a common basis, the ratio R of the generic to the reference matrix scavenging rate, generic constants overestimated probe-derived background scavenging in all three waters of Rosenfeldt and Linden (2007), by 2.5- to 11.8-fold. Against a rate-implied reference from Xiao et al. (2015), the generic model overestimated the matrix sink by 1.05- to 1.31-fold in all six conditions (equivalently, it underestimated matrix OH• by the same factor, if primary generation is correctly predicted). In four waters from Katsoyiannis et al. (2011), the sign of the error differed between matrices (R = 0.81–1.26; geometric mean 1.02, interval including unity). A one-parameter sweep shows that the DOM rate constant that reconciles the generic and measured sinks ranges from 1.97 to 3.50 × 104 L (mg C)-1 s-1 across these waters, bracketing the generic value of 2.5 × 104, and neither bulk DOM nor alkalinity ordered the error monotonically. A reconstruction of the steady-state balance against Wu and Linden (2010) reproduces the published direction and hierarchy of the CO3•- contribution. The probe-based method yields very different outcomes in the two datasets that use it, and the other methods are each represented by one dataset, so the contribution of the inference method cannot be separated from that of water and study. The findings argue against a single transferable correction factor and in favor of reporting generic-constant estimates with a matrix-specific uncertainty range.

item.title: The Ferenczy Dataset Revisited: How HIV Protease Inhibitors Created an Illusion of Universal Size Dependence in Ligand Binding
item.description: The Size‑Independent Enthalpic Efficiency (SIHE) metric normalizes binding enthalpy by molecular size and is used to compare ligands across different sizes. Re‑analyzing the Ferenczy dataset after cleaning and stratification reveals that the aggregate data exhibit an unphysical compensation slope of –1.04, which resolves into plausible slopes of –0.86 (General) and –0.75 (HIV) upon stratification. For non‑HIV targets, pKH_90 shows no meaningful correlation with molecular size (linear R2 = 0.12; power law R2 = 0.13, exponent –0.23). SIHE achieves size independence trivially because pKH is already size‑independent. The apparent size dependence in the original analysis is driven by HIV‑1 protease inhibitors, which are confined to HA = 35–50 and exhibit a distinct entropy‑driven, endothermic binding mode. Structural analysis attributes this entropy‑driven behavior to HIV‑1 protease’s non‑canonical binding site architecture (interfacial pocket, aromatic‑poor/Asp‑rich composition, glycine‑rich flap network). Formal statistical comparison (Hotelling's T2 p < 10-140) and geometric ellipse overlap (2.6%) confirm that the two subsets are largely separate. SIHE should not be used as a general metric for enthalpic efficiency.

item.title: A Single-Li+ and Electron Mixed Conductor via Intrinsic Ion-Carrier Implantation in a Metal–Organic Framework
item.description: We report a crystalline metal–organic framework (MOF) that enables efficient Li+ and electron conduction, where a triphenylene ligand functionalized with a propylsulfonate group is designed and utilized to introduce mobile Li+ ions while forming extended conjugation for electron transport. The resulting MOF exhibits a mixed conduction behavior in the solid state with a Li+ conductivity of up to 1.10 mS cm−1 and an electronic conductivity of 15.81 mS cm−1 at room temperature, together with a Li+ transference number close to 1.0. Mechanistic studies reveal that the conformationally dynamic propylsulfonate groups facilitate Li+ transport with low energy barriers in a manner resembling wobbling paddle wheels, and the rigid, conjugated scaffold promotes electronic conduction through in-plane π–d orbital coupling and interlayer interactions. This work establishes an effective bottom-up route for constructing crystalline, porous mixed Li+-electron conductors, offering a new platform for solid-state electrochemical devices requiring synchronized ion and electron transport.

item.title: In situ observation of ultra-giant spherulites in perovskite hydrates
Cellulose-Derived Cu-N-C Hybrid for Potential-Regulated CO2-to-CH4 Electroreduction
item.description: Electrochemical CO2 reduction to methane (CH4) offers a promising route for carbon utilization and renewable fuel production, yet achieving high-rate and selective CH4 formation remains challenging because of the complex multi-electron reaction pathway and the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, marine biomass-derived carbon (MBC) obtained from sea pineapple tunics is integrated with copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) to construct a CuPc/MBC hybrid for CO2 electroreduction. The optimized catalyst achieves a CH4 selectivity of 67.9%, a maximum CH4 partial current density of −538.4 mA cm-2, a CuPc-normalized mass activity of 13,460 A g-1, and stable operation for over 49 h, outperforming most previously reported Cu–N–C catalysts. Structural and spectroscopic characterization shows that the highly crystalline cellulose nanofibers form an interconnected carbon framework after vacuum carbonization, while the local Cu–N4 coordination of CuPc is largely preserved. The resulting hybrid structure promotes CuPc dispersion, electron transport, and intimate catalyst–support interfacial contact, accompanied by interfacial electronic coupling and charge redistribution. Electrochemical measurements further reveal a distinct potential dependence of CH4 selectivity, with CH4 formation and H2 evolution exhibiting opposite trends as the applied potential becomes increasingly cathodic. Density functional theory calculations indicate that more negative potentials thermodynamically favor CO2 hydrogenation toward CH4 while simultaneously enhancing the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, leading to an optimal potential window for CH4 production. This work demonstrates a sustainable molecular catalyst/carbon hybrid platform for high-rate CO2-to-CH4 electroreduction and highlights the combined roles of biomass-derived carbon architecture, catalyst–support coupling, and applied potential in regulating catalytic selectivity.

item.title: Unified reductive synthesis of pyrrole and indole under acid-free conditions
item.description: Reductive functionalization of nitrogen-bearing carboxylic acid derivatives represents a powerful yet underexplored platform for assembling value-added nitrogen heterocycles. Herein, we describe an iridium-catalyzed unified reductive manifold that converts acyclic hydrazides into pyrroles and indoles under acid-free conditions. This transformation realizes sigmatropic rearrangement via in-situ formed N,N’-dialkyl bisvinylhydrazine intermediates, circumventing key limitations of classic Piloty-Robinson and Fischer syntheses. Excellent functional-group compatibility and scale-up capability underscore its potential to expand the synthetic toolbox for carboxylic-derived nitrogen-containing molecules.

item.title: Metasurface information processor based on 4D bionic hardware and software for ultralow energy consumption computing
item.description: As AI technology faces an energy crisis, one promising solution is bionic ultra-low energy computing hardware, which can operate at a power level as low as sub-20-watt based on the 4D model of Ca 2+ channels recently verified in brain information processing. Inspired by this model, here we design and fabricate a 4D bionic computing system based on information metasurface array with the powerful capability of electromagnetic controls. Paired with specific algorithms, each metasurface cell functions as a multifunctional unit, capable of storing, regulating, transmitting, and computing information simultaneously. The metasurface array also has high energy efficiency and precision required for high-performance bionic computing. Integrated with the DNA computing, this system is expected to achieve a variety of functions including DNA replication, DNA logical computation, and DNA produce/readout. We aim to pave the way for a new paradigm in advanced computational materials that meet the evolving demands of AI and robotics.

item.title: Improving computer-aided retrosynthesis of chemically intuitive disconnections
item.description: Reliability in computer-assisted retrosynthesis relies on each architectural component. In template-based retrosynthesis, defining components include the precursor library, the trained model, and the templates. In this work, we evaluated open-source retrosynthesis tools (with default parameters), against a benchmark of 19 common disconnection strategies. An accompanying open-source dataset, template library, and trained model were developed to target simple chemistries. We investigated how precursor libraries, training data and network underfitting affect the reliability of retrosynthetic routes. A method for enumerating reaction SMIRKS into reaction SMILES is also described, providing a route to generate additional training data. The combination of an improved template library, retrained model, and expanded stock file increased the proportion of correctly solved simple case examples from 37% to 84%, outperforming all the other open-source tools. Analysis of the results showed that template presence alone is insufficient: successful retrosynthesis also depends on whether relevant templates are ranked within the search space and whether the search favours the expected route over shorter alternatives. These results highlight the importance of treating template coverage, model ranking, stock definition, and search behaviour as interacting components of retrosynthetic performance. The stock file, template library and model have been implemented into our open-source electronic lab notebook (ELN), AI4Green.

item.title: Prediction of Singlet-Triplet Gaps Using Self-Attention–Based Regression with Model Integration into a Molecular Editor
item.description: The singlet–triplet gap (STG) is an important property of photofunctional materials, but obtaining reliable values can be challenging. Experimentally, its determination often requires a combination of advanced spectroscopic techniques, while computational approaches can be time-consuming and demand specialized expertise. Therefore, a low-cost and user-friendly approach for obtaining reasonable STG estimates could make this property more accessible to non-experts. In this work, we evaluate regression models based on different molecular representations using the INVEST dataset from the Aspuru-Guzik group that contains ADC(2) energy gaps for ~70K molecules. We compare transformer models operating on SMILES representations, graph-based models (AttentiveFP), and fingerprint-based models. While AttentiveFP performs best for molecules similar to those in the training set, pre-trained transformers generalize better to unseen chemical space after fine-tuning. Motivated by these complementary strengths, we integrate our best-performing models into an online 2D chemical structure editor, enabling users to obtain STG estimates directly from drawn molecular structures. The editor can be accessed at http://ketcher-predict.ttk.hu/.

item.title: Atomic-level structure of an amorphous solid dispersion
item.description: Amorphous materials play a pivotal role across condensed-matter physics, materials science, and pharmaceuticals, for example enabling increased dissolution rates and higher in-vivo exposure for poorly bioavailable molecules. In particular, amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs), disordered multi-component mixtures of an active ingredient within a polymer matrix, are widely used to trap molecules in metastable high-energy states. However, because these systems lack longrange order, directly observing their atomic-level spatial arrangements has remained an outstanding challenge, rendering their long-term physical stability unpredictable and leaving formulation science reliant on empirical screening. Here we report the first complete three-dimensional, atomic-level structure elucidation of an amorphous solid dispersion. By combining solid-state NMR crystallography with machine-learning-accelerated quantum chemical calculations, we determine the structural ensemble of the drug AZD5462 within a copovidone matrix. We show that the polymer drives a total reconfiguration of the hydrogen-bonding network, substituting self-association with API–polymer interactions and fundamentally altering the local conformational energy landscape by raising the kinetic barriers to rearrangement. The structure explains why the formulation remains physically stable for over two years, whereas the pure amorphous drug recrystallizes within hours. These findings establish a rigorous structural framework for disordered multi-component materials, paving the way for the rational, structure-directed design of amorphous matter.

item.title: THz Calorimetry of Electrolyte Solutions Links Water’s H-Bond Network to Macroscopic Properties
item.description: Understanding the macroscopic properties of aqueous electrolyte solutions over their full solubility range requires a detailed microscopic picture of water-ion interactions. We combine THz calorimetry and dimensionality-reduction techniques to demonstrate that two to four spectroscopic markers are sufficient to describe ion-specific variations in mixing entropies and enthalpies, viscosity, and limiting conductivity across 19 electrolytes. Those markers allow us to classify electrolytes as ’strong’ or ’weak’ and report on changes in the water’s H-bond network. As concentration increases, spectroscopic nonlinearities due to ion aggregation appear that, based on a multipole expansion model for activities, are correlated with density changes. For CsI and LiCl, as prototypes of weak and strong electrolytes, respectively, the multipole expansion model accurately describes their conductivities, viscosities, and surface tensions. THz spectroscopy in combination with an activity coefficient model directly correlates macroscopic solution properties with changes in the H-bond network, paving the way towards efficient machine-learning approaches.

item.title: A grouped split silently removes the chemistry entangled with its grouping variable: the case of MOF topology hold-out
item.description: Machine learning screens metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture, and 2026 studies on enumerated databases have converged on topology hold-out as a test of topological transferability, presupposing untested separability of topology and chemistry. They are not: on hMOF (324,426 structures), 74.7% of coarse compositions (61.3% of structures) occur in a single topology, and for seven of hMOF's eleven topologies removing one topology leaves every structure with no chemical counterpart in training; the confound replicates on ARC-MOF (99.3% coarse single-topology), which is not independent of hMOF, so only a leave-one-source-out bound (98.6–99.8%) is claimed. On the isoreticular pcu ↔ nbo pair, removing the matched topology degrades nbo-side MAE by 70.0% while a sizematched control leaves it unchanged, and across the shared 25,000-sample support set the top-1% hit rate falls from 50.4% to 19.3% (five seeds). Yet the topology penalty is not explained by chemistry alone: holding out the composite chemistry key instead retains R2 = 0.674 against topology's 0.379, so the composition counts fix the identity of the withheld chemistry, not its cost. Topology hold-out should therefore not be read as a clean test of topological transferability, and grouped-split reports should first disclose the confound structure and chemical granularity, for which we provide a reporting checklist.

item.title: Grassmannian Density Learning for Physically Consistent Kohn–Sham Electronic Structure Prediction
item.description: Deep-learning electronic-structure models show great potential to accelerate first-principles calculations, with broad implications for materials science, biology and drug discovery. Yet no consensus has emerged on which physical quantity should be modeled to represent electronic states. As two fundamental quantities that arise naturally in Kohn–Sham density functional theory, the Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian and electronic density have attracted the most attention. Hamiltonian prediction, however, devotes substantial modeling capacity to degrees of freedom that do not affect the occupied electronic subspace, whereas direct regression of density matrices or real-space densities removes this redundancy but cannot ensure that the prediction represents a physically admissible electronic state. Motivated by the fact that electronic states themselves reside on a constrained manifold, we observe that predicting coordinates directly on this manifold can simultaneously eliminate redundant degrees of freedom and preserve physical admissibility. Here we introduce GeoK, a framework that predicts compact occupied–virtual orbital-rotation generators as coordinates on the manifold of electronic states, thereby ensuring each prediction corresponds to a valid electronic state of the target molecular system. We further develop a neural-network architecture tailored to this geometric prediction task. Across in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks, as well as downstream applications, GeoK consistently improves electronic-state prediction over the evaluated Hamiltonian and unconstrained densityregression baselines, while supporting robust deployment in downstream first-principles workflows. These results establish orbital-rotation generator prediction as a principled and reliable paradigm for intrinsic electronic-state modeling, opening a route towards more accurate and transferable deep-learning electronic-structure models.

item.title: Classical 1H NMR correlation rules as diagnostic tests: likelihood ratios from 168,211 experimental spectra
item.description: How much does a signal between 3.3 and 4.5 ppm say about a proton on a carbon bearing oxygen? The correlation tables used to read 1H NMR spectra state where each proton type resonates, but not how much observing, or failing to observe, a signal in that range should change a chemist’s belief. We measured this for 42 single-signal correlation rules and coupling rules transcribed from two open teaching sources, treating each rule as a diagnostic test and computing positive and negative likelihood ratios (LR+ and LR−) on two independent collections of experimental spectra with known structures: 160,038 literature peak lists from NMRexp and 8,173 atom-assigned spectra from nmrshiftdb2. Rules and scoring were frozen before the confirmatory data were examined; the sources state positions and coupling ranges, and the integration and multiplicity clauses we scored are our formalisation of what those rules imply. The rules fall into two regimes. Windows in uncrowded regions carry real evidence (aldehyde C-H LR+ 34 and 20 on the two collections, carboxylic acid O-H 11), while no window between 1.0 and 4.5 ppm exceeds LR+ 3.5 by position alone (median 1.6 and 2.3 on the two collections), because the protons of other environments occupy it: the environment a window describes accounts for a median of 20% of the assigned signals inside it. A reported integration recovers part of the crowded region (alkyl methylene LR+ 2.5 to 38), and several of the strongest effects are negative observations that the tables do not quantify (no reported signal between 6.5 and 8.0 ppm, LR− 0.011 for an aromatic C-H). The published windows are narrower than the environments they describe, and LR+ agrees between the two collections (Spearman ρ = 0.92). A coupling constant considered without regard to which signal carries it holds little information; tied to the shift region of the protons the rule concerns, in an analysis added after the confirmatory run, it gains up to thirteen-fold. In a secondary analysis in the reciprocal direction, from structure to expected shift, the additive increment rules of the standard reference tables, audited on 73,049 assigned protons, predict benzene ring protons to 0.14 ppm and protons on sp3 carbon to 0.35 ppm, with heavy-tailed errors that call for a robust likelihood. Together the results give the qualitative tables a quantitative form, measured on the information that published peak lists actually carry, that can be encoded in automated interpretation.

item.title: ProtBed: a streamlined web platform for exploratory statistics and predictive modeling in quantitative mass spectrometry
item.description: Mass spectrometry proteomics and metabolomics generate high-dimensional quantitative matrices requiring rigorous statistical and machine learning evaluation, yet existing analytical workflows typically depend on programmatic scripting or remote cloud servers that introduce datagovernance constraints. ProtBed is a client-side web application that executes post-extraction data exploration directly in the browser runtime. The platform integrates deterministic preprocessing, pairwise and omnibus hypothesis testing, six-model cross-validated machine learning, and publication-ready visualization while preserving complete local custody of quantitative abundance matrices and clinical metadata. Empirical validation was conducted across four diverse cohorts totaling 250 clinical specimens. On an untargeted GC-MS urine cohort (𝑛 = 40; 356 metabolites), stratified five-fold cross-validated classifiers discriminated diabetic kidney disease with AUC = 0.90 (89% sensitivity, 82% specificity). In a deep-coverage post-mortem substantia nigra tissue cohort (𝑛 = 30; 9,606 quantified proteins), full-matrix modeling achieved out-of-fold AUC = 0.99 using logistic regression (AUC = 0.96 for linear support vector machines) and prioritized neuroinflammatory mediators including SAA1, CRP, and GFAP. ProtBed further resolved multiclass diagnostic arms in plasma extracellular-vesicle proteomics (𝑛 = 124) and characterized dysregulated lipid classes in Alzheimer's disease plasma (𝑛 = 56). ProtBed is freely accessible at https://protbed.com/.

item.title: Fast Liquid Chromatography for Real-Time Process Monitoring of Chemical Reactions in Batch and Flow
item.description: Process analytical technologies (PATs) are increasingly vital tools in process research and development, enabling realtime monitoring of a reaction’s chemical and physical parameters. Although numerous commercial PATs exist, many are limited by sampling frequency, material consumption, or requiring unique chemical labels for spectroscopic analysis. Herein, we report a rapid, label-free analytical sampling platform that integrates fast high-pressure liquid chromatography (HPLC) with electrospray ionizationmass spectrometry (ESI-MS) for the direct, real-time monitoring of chemical reactions. Reactions are pumped into a four-port nanovolume injection valve and are injected onto short LC columns at high mobile phase flow rates, which enables chromatographic separations on the time-scale of 6–20 seconds. We demonstrate the utility of this technology by monitoring two rapid reactions relevant to the pharmaceutical industry: a photocatalytic thiol–ene reaction and a metallaphotoredox aryl sulfonamidation reaction. In each case, data-rich reaction progress profiles are obtained for monitoring the reaction progress in real-time, demonstrating the platform’s capability to deliver detailed reaction insights with minimal sample consumed (4 nL injection-1). Its modular design is adaptable to different reactor geometries and scales, while maintaining device simplicity to enable straightforward integration into existing workflows in industrial settings.

item.title: Contact organization separates biological from crystal protein interfaces matched on area and disjoint in sequence
item.description: Interface area can dominate discrimination between physiological protein interfaces and crystal contacts. We tested whether local contact organization remains informative after area matching and sequence-cluster separation. In 2,000 balanced BioMany/XtalMany interfaces, sequence cluster aware cross validation gave ROC AUC 0.904 for area and 0.937 after adding five normalized contact descriptors (difference 0.033; bootstrap 95% interval 0.015–0.058). We then fixed 40 biological and 40 crystal homomeric interfaces from the Duarte–Capitani collection, matched pairwise on area within 800–2000 Å2 and sharing no 30%-identity cluster with development. Area reached AUC 0.523; the frozen contact score reached 0.849 (dependency-component bootstrap 95% interval 0.751–0.927) and average precision 0.812. Biological interfaces carried 2.5 times the hydrophobic carbon-pair density of crystal contacts, 1.91 versus 0.76 pairs per 100 Å2. Post hoc analysis identified hydrophobic density as the main contributor; this descriptor alone reached AUC 0.829. On the same panel, unchanged PRODIGY-cryst reached AUC 0.8475 and the lineage-linked current EPPIC score reached 0.876. Contact organization therefore discriminated the curated classes after area matching and sequence-cluster separation. The inference applies to EPPIC-derived labels; protein chain size remained unmatched and associated with the score.

item.title: Controlling Vertical and Lateral Growth of Copper and Ruthenium on Tungsten Dichalcogenide Monolayers for Interconnects and Metal Contacts
item.description: The unique properties of tungsten based transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers (TMDs) drive significant interest for their use in a variety of applications, from heterogeneous catalysis, to future generation semiconductor device technologies. In these technologies the TMD monolayers are necessarily interfaced with a metal, such as a source and drain contact for use as a channel material in sub-nm transistors, an interconnect metal when used as a diffusion barrier, or as a support for a metal catalyst. The control of the morphology of the interfaced metal is critical to ensure optimal material performance for these target applications. Therefore, an atomic level description of how metals interact and grow on TMDs is needed. First principles studies of metal-TMD monolayer interactions have primarily focussed on the behaviour of single metal atom adsorption, substitutional metal doping, or pristine metal-monolayer interfaces. Consequently, there persists a clear gap in the understanding of metal growth on TMD monolayers and the drivers of vertical versus lateral growth. In this work, we present a density functional theory and ab initio molecular dynamics investigation of the adsorption, preferred morphology, and dynamics of Cu and Ru metal deposits on WS2 and WSe2 monolayers. Using metal cluster models of sufficient size to display a variety of potential morphologies, and by characterising the behaviour of the metal deposits with an ensemble of analytical shape descriptors derived from the gyration tensor, we develop a comprehensive and quantitative understanding of the structure, stability, dynamics, and morphology of deposited metals on tungsten TMD monolayers. We find that on both TMDs Cu prefers to form compact, vertically growing clusters, with molecular dynamics simulations showing a transition to a more compact metal shape and a further promotion of 3D growth over time. In contrast, Ru prefers to grow laterally on WS2. Ru present on WSe2 displays a preference for a lateral morphology as on WS2, but makes noticeably more compact deposits on WSe2 than on WS2. Dynamics simulations show that temperature further promotes growth in the preferred direction, thus driving both island growth and lateral deposition depending on the inherent preference for a growth mode. These results demonstrate clearly how the identity of the metal and the TMD layer contribute to the preferred growth mode and morphology. Additionally, we reveal the critical importance of dynamic cluster evolution over time in determining the final structure.

item.title: DeImmu-MPNN: Reducing Immunogenicity in De Novo Protein Design
item.description: De novo-designed proteins lack an evolutionary history of immune tolerance, making antidrug antibody (ADA) responses a barrier to their clinical translation. ProteinMPNN is widely used to design sequences for a given protein backbone, but it does not account for immune tolerance, which is important for therapeutic applications. The ADA response to injected proteins is driven principally by MHC class II presentation of protein-derived peptides to CD4+ T-helper cells. We fine-tuned ProteinMPNN using direct preference optimization to reduce ADA-relevant class II epitopes across a six-allele HLA-DRB1 panel, while also reducing class I epitopes. The resulting model, DeImmu-MPNN, reduces NetMHCIIpan-predicted MHC class II presentation by 41.4% relative to the baseline model, bringing predicted presentation to the level of length-matched human proteins, and NetMHCpan-predicted MHC class I presentation by 33.0% on the same designs, for 2.1 points of sequence recovery and no detectable structural cost. The reduction transfers without retraining to unseen DRB1 alleles, the DRB3/4/5 paralogs, and HLA-DQ. It generalizes to 11 published de novo binder complexes, with mean reductions of 50.4% for class II and 30.2% for class I and no systematic predicted cost to interface confidence. DeImmu-MPNN provides a framework for incorporating immune presentation into protein sequence design and may dramatically facilitate the design of proteins with reduced immunogenicity.

item.title: FluorCast: Solvent-aware 2D-3D feature fusion for predicting fluorophore photophysics
item.description: Machine-learning (ML) models can accelerate the prediction of fluorescence properties, but their apparent performance depends strongly on molecular representation and on the evaluation strategy. Here we present FluorCast, a solvent-aware ML framework assembled from three public datasets—ChemFluor, Deep4Chem, and FluoDB-Lite—comprising 66,820 standardized records, 33,965 unique chromophores, and 1,368 nonmissing canonical environment identifiers. Conventional Morganfingerprint models were benchmarked for absorption and emission maxima, photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), and Stokes shift under random, molecule-grouped, and scaffold-grouped splits, revealing substantial performance degradation with increasing structural novelty. To incorporate three-dimensional (3D) molecular information, we evaluated frozen 512-dimensional ConforFormer embeddings alone and in feature-level fusion with Morgan fingerprints. On matched test sets, fusion reduced the mean absolute error (MAE) relative to Morgan fingerprints alone in 11 of 12 target-split combinations, although molecule-grouped PLQY prediction worsened and several scaffold-grouped gains were small. An external set of five recently reported fluorophores with no exact training-set match provided a further test; fusion reduced absorption MAE from 65.67 to 24.49 nm, whereas Morgan-only models performed better for emission and Stokes shift, and PLQY performance was comparable. These results indicate that learned 3D conformational embeddings provide complementary, target-dependent information rather than a universal replacement for two-dimensional (2D) molecular fingerprints.

item.title: Evaluation of Reusable Monolithic Silica Columns for Sustainable Liquid Chromatography in Organic Synthesis
item.description: Liquid chromatography (LC) is essential for compound purification in synthetic organic chemistry. However, single-use particle-packed columns using silica gel result in substantial solvent and solid waste. We herein evaluate reusable monolithic silica gel columns as a practical and sustainable alternative, based on 370 purification runs conducted by 14 researchers over one year under routine laboratory conditions. Compared to conventional particle-packed columns, the monolithic system was estimated to reduce annual LC solvent consumption by 74% and solid silica waste by 95%, while maintaining high separation performance even for challenging separations (e.g., ΔRf < 0.1). A modeled life cycle assessment (LCA) further indicated that total CO2 emissions and energy consumption per purification were reduced by over 80%, primarily due to reduced solvent use. A modeled workflow analysis indicated an approximately 40% reduction in purification time relative to manual purification using self-packed particle columns. Analysis of the recorded monolith data showed no clear relationship between user experience and solvent consumption. The plate efficiency of the monolithic columns was comparable to that of preparative high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) columns packed with 10 μm particles, despite operating at a low gauge pressure of 0.1 bar. Requiring only standard laboratory equipment, this reusable system combines high separation performance with reduced solvent consumption, minimal solid waste, and improved operational efficiency. By substantially reducing the resources and labor required for routine purification without sacrificing separation performance, this technology has the potential to make synthetic organic chemistry more efficient and environmentally sustainable.

item.title: Two extrapolation axes decide whether interaction needs a module in many-body systems
item.description: We separate the extrapolation problem in many-body systems into two axes: toward combinations with more components (the composition axis), and toward components unseen (the identity axis). The prevailing pipeline—encode then interact—performs poorly when extrapolating in composition count. We open an interaction-free route to interaction by strengthening its encoder until a component’s representation can carry what it contributes across the mixtures it appears in. Where component identities are bounded while their combinations are not, this route performs better along the composition axis, while the prevailing route is better along the identity axis; both differences follow from the functional forms rather than from the data. Chemical mixtures are the main example, synthetic tasks isolate the two axes, and the same structure recurs in other fields.

item.title: Approaching the Two-Dimensional Limit of the S = 1/2 Kagome Magnet via Metal-Organic Framework Exfoliation
item.description: Realising chemically programmable two-dimensional magnetic materials is a major challenge in the development of next-generation quantum technologies. Layered magnetic metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) provide an attractive platform because their reticular design enables systematic control over composition, topology, and magnetic interactions while offering the possibility of exfoliation into atomically thin nanosheets. Here, we investigate the layered S = 1/2 kagome MOF, Cu3(CO3)2(bipy)6 · 2 ClO4, whose bulk magnetic structure is most consistently described by ferromagnetic kagome layers that are ferromagnetically correlated to adjacent ones. We develop a micromechanical Scotch tape exfoliation strategy capable of producing few-layer nanosheets and combine synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) to demonstrate that the Cu2+ oxidation state and ferromagnetic behaviour are retained following exfoliation. By showing that magnetic functionality is preserved in the exfoliated kagome MOF nanosheets, this work establishes the promise of layered magnetic MOFs as tuneable platforms for low-dimensional quantum magnetism and provides an important experimental route toward realising the archetypal S = 1/2 kagome magnet in the two-dimensional limit.

item.title: Myxobacterial terpene synthases produce structurally diverse sesquiterpenes
item.description: Myxobacteria represent an underexplored source of terpenoids with relatively few terpenoids and terpene synthases known from this phylum. Thirteen sesquiterpenes (1–13) representing ten distinct carbon skeletons were identified from eight myxobacterial terpene synthases. Twelve of these natural products (1–10, 12, and 13), including enantiomers of known brasilane-type sesquiterpenes (1–3) and the humulene analog viticumulin A (4), were previously unknown from myxobacteria. Moreover, ten (i.e., 1–4, 7–10, 12, 13) have not been previously reported from bacterial sources. These data demonstrate that myxobacteria represent a rich and largely untapped reservoir of terpenoids that should be further investigated.

item.title: Lithium Polysulfide Speciation in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries: A First-Principles Benchmark of Thermodynamics, Bonding, and Solvent Control
item.description: Lithium–sulfur cycle life is limited by dissolved LiyS q x polysulfides whose speciation remains disputed. We benchmark the complete matrix (y = 0–2, q = 0 to −2, x = 1–8) in the gas phase, tetraglyme and dimethyl sulfoxide: 248 M06-2X/SMD thermochemistries, 132 refined by single-point CCSD. The convex hull, S8 → Li2S6 → Li2S4 → Li2S3 → Li2S2 → Li2S, is identical in both solvents, and every exergonic long-chain comproportionation delivers Li2S6. QTAIM analysis of the CCSD densities separates covalent S–S from electrostatic Li–S bonding, transferably between solvents. Solvation makes S 2–x the dominant lithium-free 1 charge state and places both legs of the shuttle on that branch. Infrared and Raman spectra of prepared solutions test the vibrational predictions and track the chain-length distribution through one band envelope. The open dataset is a calibrated reference for force-field, machine-learned and continuum battery models.

item.title: Steroid Thioesters to Target Golgi Apparatus
item.description: Despite Golgi apparatus plays a central role in lipid and protein trafficking, the biomedical potential of Golgitargeting supramolecular assemblies remains underexplored. While recent studies showed that peptide thioesters localize to the Golgi, it is unclear whether steroid thioesters can exhibit similar targeting behavior. Here, we designed and synthesized steroid-based thioesters by conjugating a thioester group and an NBD fluorophore to bile acids (BAs). Live-cell fluorescence imaging revealed that steroid thioesters localize to the Golgi apparatus, further confirming the utility of thioesters as a reactive warhead for Golgi targeting via localized S-palmitoylation. While BA-thioesters accumulate at the Golgi, their accumulation is slower than peptide thioesters. Unlike the peptide thioesters, these steroid conjugates displayed excellent cellular compatibility, showing minimal cytotoxicity. O-acetylation of BAs also modulates the dynamics of Golgi targeting. Our findings demonstrate that steroid thioesters can serve as Golgi-targeting motifs, expanding the pool of organelle-directed bioconjugates and providing a new scaffold for the design of functional molecules to reprogram palmitoylation-associated processes.

item.title: Spin-chemistry modulation of ATP synthesis via vibronic reorganisation
item.description: Coordination between adenosine diphosphate (ADP) and a magnesium (Mg) ion is a key prerequisite step in the synthesis of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), and in the last few decades it has been proposed that ATP synthesis yields may be sensitive to magnetic fields. Prior studies have invoked the radical-pair mechanism to explain magnetic field effects (MFEs) and magnetic isotope effects (MIEs) in ATP synthases; however, the microscopic conditions required for such effects have not been clearly established. Here, we investigate the mechanistic constraints under which MFEs and MIEs may emerge in the ADP-Mg precursory complex through spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and the hyperfine interaction. Enhanced triplet populations, key to preventing recombination, are observed only upon isotopic enrichment. We find that isotope-dependent vibronic reorganisation dominates spin evolution in the ADP-Mg radical pair, contrary to the conventional interpretation that magnetic isotope effects originate from nuclear-spin-dependent hyperfine interactions. While the MFE was found to be negligible, spin-dynamics simulations reveal a 45% enhancement in projected ATP yields due to MIEs. Molecular dynamics simulations show that perturbations to the dimer conformation and Mg coordination environment do not strongly alter the spin chemistry. These results reconcile the conflicting observations of magnetosensitivity in ATP synthesis and establish experimentally testable criteria for assessment of field-sensitive bioenergetic systems.

item.title: Combinatorial Steiner Methodology for Efficiently Exploring Chemical Space in CO2 Hydrogenation to Fischer-Tropsch Reactivity via High-throughput Experimentation
item.description: High-throughput experimentation (HTE) and machine learning (ML) have accelerated discovery in molecular chemistry. Meanwhile, such advances in heterogeneous catalysis are hindered by the complexity of materials and the vast chemical space. We present a mathematically optimized methodology using Steiner coverings to explore multi-component catalysts and access lower-dimension interactions through higher-dimension blocks. From 21 elements, we designed a library of 70 trimetallic mixed-metal-oxide catalysts, covering all 210 possible bimetallic pairs. The experimental workflow was automated by a robotic platform and applied to thermocatalytic CO2 hydrogenation, critical for achieving a circular carbon economy. In just 70 materials we successfully recovered and uncovered trends in methanation, reverse water–gas shift (RWGS), and methanol synthesis, while discovering a highly active FeGaRu catalyst for CO2–Fischer–Tropsch synthesis that retains this reactivity when simplified to binary FeRu, Ga providing improved performances. Our combinatorial optimization methodology replaces thousands of manual experiments with strategic exploration, improving the discovery rate for complex, multi-component heterogeneous catalysts.

item.title: Single-Ion Hydration Through the Lens of Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials
item.description: Single-ion hydration provides a stringent test of molecular models because local ionwater interactions, collective polarization, nuclear quantum effects, and long-range electrostatics all contribute to experimentally measurable structure, spectra, and thermodynamics. Here we discuss how data-driven many-body potentials, in particular MB-pol for water and MB-nrg for hydrated ions, provide a physically transparent route from correlated electronic structure data to predictive simulations of ion hydration from clusters to bulk water and aqueous interfaces. We emphasize how this framework transforms single-ion hydration from a parameterization problem into a hierarchy of many-body observables, and we outline opportunities for connecting simulations directly with interfacial spectroscopy, hydration free energies, and complex electrolyte environments.

item.title: A Hierarchical Latent Architecture of the Chemical Bond Revealed
item.description: The chemical bond has no unique quantum-mechanical observable, and energetic, orbital/wavefunction, 9 and electron-density analyses can therefore agree, specialize, or apparently conflict. In this work, we ask 10 whether unsupervised machine learning can reveal a simpler physicochemical organization beneath this 11

item.title: Directional Control of Droplet Motion via Geometric Gating
item.description: We explore new methods for inducing the movement of water droplets on elastomeric substrates, such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Our approach builds upon the well-known phenomenon that water droplets move easily across these substrates when swelled with silicone oil. While designing shallow open channels and traps on a PDMS film offers a simple way to control a droplet's trajectory by tilting the substrate in two orthogonal directions, this method is poorly suited for manipulating multiple droplets simultaneously. To address this limitation, we introduce two new methods. The first method utilizes a piano-concave PDMS platform with a radius of curvature significantly larger than the size of the droplet and its translation distance. When the system's configuration is altered, this curved substrate consistently guides the droplet along a curved geodesic. The second method incorporates diode-like gates on the PDMS. These gates are created on either flat or piano-concave PDMS films by embedding thin, rigid plates into the elastomer prior to crosslinking, followed by swelling in silicone oil. This process generates sigmoidal steps that restrict droplet motion to a single direction. Finally, we demonstrate how combining these two strategies enables various forms of directed motion for both single and multiple droplets.

item.title: Vegetation-Rainfall Relationship within the Caatinga Biome
item.description: With drought and extreme weather events increasing in frequency, it has become crucial to understand the relation between weather and biome responses. The semi-arid Caatinga biome of Brazil is highly sensitive to climatic variability, and particularly to changes in precipitation and drought frequency. This study explores a remote-sensing workflow to estimate green vegetation cover and assess its relationship with precipitation using satellite imagery. Monthly satellite composites were processed to distinguish green and non-green vegetation, comparing the efficacy between a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a python classification method. We match the computational measurements of green vegetation cover with monthly precipitation data from the four nearest weather stations. Green cover analysis shows a lagged positive relationship with precipitation, with wetter months generally exhibiting greater green vegetation coverage. The study demonstrates the potential of combining satellite imagery, CNN classification and climatic data for longterm remote ecosystem monitoring.

item.title: Polarization-Driven Hydride Transfer Promotes Cobalt Tetrasulfophthalocyanine-Catalyzed Hydrogen Evolution by Five Orders of Magnitude
item.description: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains unclear how adsorption affects M-H hydricity. Herein, we quantitatively compare the catalytic activity and mechanism of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) from cobalt tetrasulfophthalocyanine (CoTSPc) in a dissolved aqueous form (CoTSPc(aq)) and when adsorbed to the surface of a carbon electrode (CoTSPc/C). At the same electrode potential, CoTSPc/C catalyzes HER at a rate that is over five orders of magnitude faster than CoTSPc(aq). Mechanistic studies indicate that both CoTSPc/C and CoTSPc(aq) catalyze HER via a rate-limiting hydride transfer to a proton donor in solution to form H2. Hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc(aq) is a purely chemical step defined by a constant hydricity of 22.4 kcal mol−1 that is independent of applied potential. In contrast, hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc/C is strongly polarization dependent, decreasing hydricity by ~23 kcal mol−1 V−1 to values as low as 1.2 kcal mol−1 at −1.1 V vs SHE, leading to the observed rate promotion. We attribute this mechanistic change to the positioning of the CoTSPc-H intermediate within the electrochemical double layer, such that the hydride traverses the interfacial electrostatic potential difference during the RLS. These results demonstrate the power of surface adsorption to generate highly reactive molecular hydrides and fundamentally reshape the free energy landscape of electrocatalysis.

item.title: Solvotaxis: Gel Motion Against Gravity via Autonomous Solvent Exchange
item.description: Molecular gelation, where a low-molecular-weight gelator (LMWG) self-assembles into a network of fibers, has long obeyed a simple rule: a solvent can be gelled only if the gelator is at least partially soluble in it. In this work, we overturn this paradigm and show that the disaccharidebased gelator 4′,6′-O-benzylidene amygdalin (BA) forms stable gels in solvents where it is completely insoluble. BA dissolves in aqueous media upon heating and forms hydrogels upon cooling, but it is insoluble and does not form gels in oils. When an immiscible nonpolar oil is placed atop a BA hydrogel, the network spontaneously absorbs the oil, expels the water, and migrates upward against gravity. At steady state, a stable BA organogel sits atop liquid water. We refer to this process as Autonomous Solvent Exchange (ASE) and it reveals a strong preference of BA fibers for oil over water (whereas BA molecules prefer water). ASE thus leads to the unusual phenomenon of solvotaxis, i.e., migration of the gel toward its preferred solvent without disrupting the fibrous network. BA organogels with tunable strengths can be formed by solvotaxis across a range of oils (e.g., n-alkanes, natural oils, fuels). Overall, by decoupling molecular solubility from gelation, solvotaxis expands the landscape of gelation to previously inaccessible liquids. Our work also establishes new principles for designing materials that respond autonomously to chemical gradients, with potential applications in environmental remediation and oil recovery.

item.title: Triple Atom Transfer-Enabled α-C(sp3)-H Aminomethylation of Aliphatic Amines: General and Modular Access to Vicinal Diamines
item.description: Vicinal diamines are prevalent structural elements in organic molecules. In particular, those featuring a tertiary alkylamine motif are commonly found in biologically active molecules and therapeutic agents. However, methods for the efficient construction of these architectures from inexpensive and readily available feedstocks remain scarce. Here, we report a mild photocatalytic protocol for the modular synthesis of vicinal alkyl diamines via triple atom transfer-enabled α-C(sp3)–H aminomethylation. This transformation integrates halogen-atom transfer (XAT) and intramolecular 1,5-hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) processes to furnish key α-amido alkyl radicals, which subsequently add to in situ-generated iminium ions. Critical to the success of the reaction is the cooperative action of a nickel complex and a zinc salt, which jointly promote the aminomethylation process. Utility of this method is demonstrated through late-stage modification of complex amine molecules, scale-up experiments, and ready access to scaffold-diverse free vicinal diamines. In addition, compatibility with aromatic aldehydes and the ability to functionalize alternative C–H sites further expand the chemical space of diamine architectures, highlighting the robustness and synthetic versatility of this protocol.

item.title: Nature skips the 3/2 rung: point group selects the orientational exponent
item.description: The low-temperature orientational heat capacity of an interacting multipole pair is conventionally taken to be two-valued: 3/2 k_B for axially symmetric moments and 2 k_B otherwise. Here I evaluate it for all 101,666,280 molecular geometries of the OMol25 dataset and show that this is the bottom rung of a staircase: the exponent is a count, not a case split, γ = C_v/k_B = Σ_i 1/p_i, which for two rigid nonlinear molecules is exactly γ = D/2 and leaves only the rungs 3/2, 2 and 5/2. Of 11,325,000 pairs drawn uniformly from the whole dataset none occupies the 3/2 rung (P < 3.26×10⁻⁷), and the rest split 12.05% and 87.95% between γ = 2 and 5/2, so nearly the whole molecular world shares one coefficient: (5/2) k_B = 20.79 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ per mole of pairs. The rung is deleted structurally rather than thermally suppressed: axiality is forced only by a C₃ or higher rotation axis in the equilibrium point group, and a census of equilibrium structures weighted by the dataset's own size distribution bounds the branch at 2.07×10⁻⁵ — a limit set by symmetry rather than by a numerical threshold, and therefore independent of how the geometries were sampled; and which rung a pair occupies is settled by its point group at the dominant multipole rank rather than by temperature, coupling or size — a C₃ axis supplies axiality only at rank two, so the bottom rung needs σ_h or S₆ as well.

item.title: Does Endocrine State Gate Proteoform-Induced Synaptic Vulnerability? A Metaplasticity Framework for Menopause and Early Neurodegeneration
item.description: This is a hypothesis-driven conceptual review, not a systematic review or meta-analysis, integrating two largely independent bodies of neuroscience literature — the neuroendocrinology of the menopause transition and the molecular synaptotoxicity of soluble amyloid-β (Aβ) oligomers — to ask whether they converge on a shared synaptic mechanism. Estrogen (17β-estradiol) and the neurosteroid allopregnanolone regulate hippocampal excitatory-inhibitory balance through ERβ, GPER1, and GABA-A δ-subunit-containing receptors, although not uniformly through “anti-LTD”: GPER1 mediates its own distinct form of long-term depression (LTD). Separately, soluble, preplaque Aβ oligomers facilitate NMDA receptor- and mGluR1-dependent hippocampal LTD via convergent calcineurin/AKAP150 spine elimination signaling, independent of amyloid plaques. We situate both literatures within Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro (BCM) metaplasticity theory, in which a sliding modification threshold, not a fixed switch, governs whether a synaptic input produces potentiation or depression. We propose a specific, falsifiable hypothesis: that decreasing estrogen/allopregnanolone tone and increasing proteoform burden act on convergent postsynaptic machinery to jointly lower this threshold in the hippocampal and limbic circuits. We explicitly distinguish this synaptic-level claim from the clinically separate phenomena of perimenopausal mood symptoms, subjective cognitive complaints, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer's disease and weigh it against four competing models, including the possibility that endocrine decline and proteinopathy are both downstream of a shared upstream process. We present a structured, falsifiable research agenda specifying the experiments needed to confirm, partially confirm, or refute the proposed convergence. We do not claim that the central hypothesis is established; our contribution is to make an underexplored cross-disciplinary link explicit and testable.

item.title: Martini 3 Coarse-Grained Models for Steroid Hormones
item.description: Steroid hormones are central to the development, metabolism, homeostasis and reproduction of animals and have been the subject of many evolutionary, ecotoxicological and human health studies. Coarse-grain molecular dynamics (CG MD) simulations are a powerful tool to study the structural and dynamic behavior of steroid hormones and their interactions. Here, we expand the capabilities of the widely used Martini 3 CG framework by parameterizing and validating a set of 20 steroid hormone models — including both endogenous and synthetic molecules — to enable their study across diverse targets, systems, and fields of interest.Hormone parameterization followed Martini 3 guidelines, while leveraging the similarities with the parent cholesterol molecule, for which a Martini 3 model is available. Notably, we were able to base our parameterization on the hundreds of experimental structures in the protein data bank that contain steroid hormones, instead of relying on atomistic simulations as is typical with Martini.The parameterized models match to within 5% target molecular volumes, and recover the overall hydrophobicity trend of the hormones, although higher hydrophobicities tended to be overestimated. In free simulations of protein-hormone systems the experimentally known binding poses could be recovered for 89% of the cases, indicating a successful parameterization also from a functional standpoint. Since several Martini 3 protein models were tested, we also incidentally show that the flexibility of the OLIVES and GōMartini models makes them best suited for this type of protein–ligand recognition. Finally, models were validated in interaction with membranes by comparison to reference atomistic data.We expect that the availability of our fully validated Martini 3 CG steroid hormone models will contribute to new studies, collaborations, and applications across different scientific fields.

item.title: Electrolyte Switching Reveals Electric Double Layer Dynamics and Electrocatalytic Electrolyte Effects
item.description: New insights into the electric double layer (EDL) under strongly driven electrocatalytic (EC) conditions are obtained by measuring its rearrangement kinetics in response to abrupt switching of bulk electrolyte composition (55 ms for complete exchange up to the ordered layers of the EDL) The aqueous alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is used as a model EC system, motivated by its opposite alkali metal hydroxide effect: catalyst activity decreases with increasing cation radius on Pt (Li+ > Na+ > K+ > Cs+) whereas the trend is opposite for Au and Ag. Monitoring the constant potential HER current as the electrolyte composition is switched between two different cations (e.g. Li+ and Cs+) provides an overall kinetic picture as the EDL rearranges to accommodate the new cation. For both Pt, Au, and Ag, the transition time is asymmetric; switching from a smaller ionic radius to a larger one is faster than the reverse (e.g. 95 ± 31 ms for Li+ → K+ compared to 352 ± 38 ms for K+ → Li+ on Pt at -200 mV vs RHE). Transition times also increase with greater ionic radius difference between the cations and at more negative potentials. The transition time trends are consistent with more weakly hydrated cations having stronger electrostatic ion-electrode interactions and hence being slower to leave. EDL rearrangement kinetics appear unaffected by the simultaneously occurring HER. Mixing LiOH with the stickier K/CsOH electrolytes produced a smooth, continuous variation in HER kinetics with increasing K/CsOH fraction on Pt, Au, and Ag, even though we expect the closest ion plane (CIP) to be mostly K+/Cs+ over the range. This shows that EDL structure beyond the CIP can also influence HER kinetics on Pt, Au, and Ag. Our work emphasizes the spatial extent of electrolyte influence which needs to be captured by theory.

item.title: Obstructions to four-body perimetric coordinates
item.description: Pekeris’ perimetric coordinates make the three-body Coulomb problem tractable. They are linear in the interparticle distances, range independently over [0,∞), and turn the Schrödinger equation into a sparse recursion. Whether a four-body analogue exists has been debated since 1966, with claims in both directions and no agreed definition. We formulate a hierarchy of definitions and settle each level of it. (i) No linear coordinates exist, because the configuration domain is not convex. (ii) No coordinates smooth up to the boundary, in the sense of a diffeomorphism of manifolds with corners, exist even locally, because the domain has a round tangent cone at collinear configurations. (iii) Independent coordinates on the closed orthant whose squared distances are polynomial do exist. They cover the whole domain and are bijective on its interior. Degree 4 is attained. (iv) No independent coordinates exist in which the six distances themselves are rational functions, for instance polynomials. The proof of (iv) shows that the variety of coplanar configurations, written in the distances, is birational to a quotient (X ×X)/G of the square of a Kummer K3 surface. It therefore carries a nonzero holomorphic 4-form and cannot be parametrized rationally. Finally, we identify an exact Galois symmetry in a broad class of Pekeris-type sparse schemes, the coefficientwise graded schemes. If one distance enters only through its square, such a scheme computes identical spectra for repulsion and for attraction in that pair, so it cannot converge for both. If it is consistent for the attractive problem, it has spurious eigenvalues below the true ground state of the repulsive one. A helium calculation exhibits this behaviour. Within this class, uniform convergence for four-body Coulomb systems therefore requires rational distances, which (iv) excludes. Every computational step is accompanied by a runnable check.

item.title: Galvanic Coupling Links Heterogeneous and Molecular Palladium Catalysis in Aerobic Alcohol Oxidation
item.description: Thermochemical catalytic reactions are often composed of coupled electrochemical redox reactions, which may even generate the active catalyst itself. Here we show that oxygen reduction on heterogeneous palladium drives corrosion of Pd(0) through galvanic coupling: electrons released by Pd(0) oxidation are consumed by oxygen reduction on the same catalyst, and the soluble Pd(II) forms a homogeneous complex which catalyzes benzyl alcohol oxidation. Combining corrosion measurements with quantification of Pd(II) and reaction products, we find that supplying more oxygen raises the catalyst potential and accelerates Pd(II) generation and alcohol oxidation. Applying equivalent electrochemical potentials in the absence of oxygen reproduces Pd(II) generation and alcohol oxidation with similar sensitivity to the catalyst potential. Diverting the anodic reaction to a sacrificial anode suppresses Pd(II) supply and thus the thermochemical reaction rate. Hence, the primary role of oxygen is to set the potential for generating the active catalyst, while palladium corrosion is the kinetic link to thermochemical turnover. Together, our results show that galvanic coupling provides a framework that links electrochemistry and thermochemical catalysis.

item.title: Expanding Non-Natural Prenyl Diphosphate Chemical Space through Promiscuous yet Regioselective C2-Methylation
item.description: Prenyl diphosphate methyltransferases are emerging as powerful biocatalysts that bypass the classic isoprene rule, installing methyl appendages directly onto standard (iso)prenyl diphosphate substrates and transforming conventional terpene architectures into non-canonical terpenoids. Although their activity toward natural precursors is well documented, their biocatalytic tolerance toward non-natural analogs remains largely underexplored. Here, we systematically probe the substrate scope of the C2-geranyl diphosphate methyltransferase from Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2) (ScGPP-MT) using a library of 40 structurally diverse synthetic allylic, benzylic and heterocyclic diphosphate (alkyl-PP) analogs spanning 4–15 carbons. Direct screening revealed that 10 analogs serve as substrates, including the natural substrate geranyl diphosphate (GPP), establishing a minimum linear chain length of seven carbons for acceptance. To expand this scope, we developed a coupled enzymatic cascade with Lithospermum erythrorhizon GPP synthase (LeGPPS), in which non-natural GPP derivatives are generated by condensation of synthetic alkyl-PP analogs with isopentenyl diphosphate (IPP) and subsequently methylated by ScGPP-MT. This cascade successfully processed 25 additional analogs, including the natural substrate. Collectively, ScGPP-MT accommodates allylic substrates spanning 7–11 linear carbons from diphosphate headgroup, enabling modification of 33 distinct non-natural analogs. To investigate the regiochemistry of ScGPP-MT-catalyzed methylation, which cannot be directly determined because methylated prenyl diphosphates and their alcohol derivatives are difficult to isolate, we coupled the methylation reaction with an engineered aromatic prenyltransferase, NphB(M31S), affording an array of structurally unique, non-canonical cannabinoid precursors. Scale-up and subsequent structural characterization of selected cannabinoid precursors revealed that ScGPP-MT is strictly regio-specific, performing C2-methylation of non-natural substrates just as it does with GPP. Together, these results establish a versatile biocatalytic platform that circumvents traditional biosynthetic constraints, offering a powerful toolkit for the de novo synthesis of diverse unnatural terpenoids with potential pharmaceutical value.

item.title: Hexanitrogen (N6) formation via direct dinitrogen activation
item.description: Dinitrogen (N2), the major component of air is the only nitrogen allotrope found in nature. Due to its exceptional stability, its activation is rather challenging but a key step in N2 fixation as, for example, in the Haber-Bosch process.1–3 In Earth’s atmosphere, N2 is continuously activated through energetic processes that drive its chemistry away from equilibrium toward reactive nitrogen species. This activation has long inspired efforts to synthetically replicate these energetic processes and elucidate the underlying activation mechanisms. Here we present the formation of the C2h-N6 nitrogen allotrope (in short N6) through direct N2 activation. N6 was previously prepared starting from metal azides.4 In the present work, we continuously irradiated gaseous N2 with an electron beam at 200 eV under flow conditions, followed by co-deposition onto a cold window at 3.5 K. In such experiments, we detected N6 alongside oxygen-containing and atmospherically relevant nitrogen-oxo species and O3. The formation of N6 under such conditions establishes a new route to its formation directly from N2, thereby providing direct access to a neutral nitrogen allotrope that holds potential as a high-energy-density material.

item.title: TENKi: counting the value of borrowed knowledge to a materials campaign in measurements saved
item.description: Materials campaigns draw on data of very different cost: a band gap costs almost nothing from a database, core-hours from a hybrid-functional density functional theory (DFT) calculation, and instrument time from a measurement. No calibration carries values from low-cost to costly sources, and multi-fidelity methods do not state how many costly evaluations an imported ordering of the candidates replaces. We test whether that ordering, with its margins, reduces the evaluations needed to reach a given ranking quality, and whether the saving can be measured for each route. TENKi (Transfer-ensemble Knowledge Inheritance) records ranking agreement against budget while a ranking model is fitted to queries that order several candidates at once, with the donor ordering entered as a prior whose trust is learned from incoming results. The evidence is 261,053 archived band-gap records from eight sources, 171 semiconductors with gaps computed on demand, and an aluminium–magnesium–silicon (Al–Mg–Si) alloy pool computed with DFT and molecular dynamics. Queries ranking four candidates outperform pairwise comparisons on every source, a donor prior replaces nearly half of the early measurement budget, and a trained query-selection policy reaches the ranking quality of random selection with fewer evaluations on held-out sources, whereas hand-written rules do not. An ordering from the generalised gradient approximation cuts hybrid-functional compute about sixfold, while an archived ordering that lacks the alloys gives no saving at fixed trust; for Al–Mg–Si, a foundation-potential ordering lowers the DFT compute needed to find eight of the ten most stable compounds from 19% to 5%. The saving depends on direction and coverage, and the agreement-versus-budget curve separates disagreement that further sampling removes from gaps that remain, so a campaign can use these curves to decide which source to compute first, how far to trust it, and when further evaluations stop improving the ranking.

item.title: Graded revision lets autonomous campaigns update symbolic laws of SiGeC semiconductors from mixed-fidelity evidence
item.description: Autonomous materials campaigns combine published measurements, simulations at several levels of theory and curated compilations whose errors are known in kind but not in size. A value off the current law may be an error, a measurement under a special condition, or a lead to missing physics, and an outlier filter discards all three alike. Machine unlearning removes data from neural networks by costly or approximate retraining, and provenance records locate data origins without identifying which conclusions to revise. We tested whether nine graded revision actions on sourcetagged evidence, from labelling or reweighting rows to forgetting them, confine each correction to conclusions named in advance. The actions operate on symbolic laws fitted by HG-SR, a symbolic-regression engine whose terms record their supporting evidence, and were applied to the lattice thermal conductivity of Si1-xGex and SiGeC, which limits heat removal from SiGe transistors. The pipeline corrected an undesigned unit error, caught mislabelled and amorphous simulation rows from their structure, split the literature by microstructure and issued a conductivity law with a declared validity domain. Of twelve decisions on flagged values, four found errors; the other eight kept the value, five as special conditions (microstructure, another alloy, melting, box size, nonlinear response) and three as leads to physics the law lacked. For SiGeC it showed that carbon leaves the lattice as SiC and named in advance the one weak input of the germanium-saving claim; pre-registered tests of that input changed only the named conclusions for a leg operated from 300 to 1100 K, leaving its composition and carbon content unchanged. Because the SiC scattering contrast fell with particle radius roughly as R−4, 2.5 nm SiC replaces 14–16% of the germanium at equal lattice thermal conductivity (8–9% at 5 nm). Corrections become targeted errata, not rebuilds, and less germanium eases demand for a by-product metal of constrained supply.

item.title: Evaluating transfer across modalities in autonomous materials systems
